title: Best Laundry Room Dehumidifier (2026): Drain-Ready Picks
dek: Your laundry room already has the plumbing a dehumidifier wants. Hook one up to the standpipe and forget about musty towels for good.
description: The best laundry room dehumidifier for every setup: units that drain into the standpipe, shrug off lint and fit a stacked-washer closet or open mudroom.
intro: A **laundry room dehumidifier** has a tougher job than you might think. Every wash load releases moisture into the air, a dryer with a leaky or kinked vent adds more, and many laundry rooms have no window and little air exchange with the rest of the house. Humidity can climb high enough to fog a window or start mildew behind the machines within days.

The good news: laundry rooms usually have exactly what a dehumidifier needs — a **standpipe, utility sink or floor drain** a few feet away. Run a hose into it once, and the unit drains itself forever. Our top pick is a compact 22-pint Frigidaire with a lint-friendly filter and a continuous-drain port; we've also picked a pump model for rooms without a low drain, a space-saver for stacked closets and a bigger unit for laundry areas that open onto a basement or mudroom.
Before you buy, check the dryer vent. A disconnected or crushed duct can dump a gallon or more of water vapor into the room per load, and no dehumidifier should have to fight that.
topPicksLead: The **Frigidaire FFAD2233W1** is our top pick for most laundry rooms because it's right-sized, quiet and built to drain straight into a nearby standpipe.

What you'll empty with a hose into the standpipe

blocks.text: The EPA recommends 30–50% humidity indoors. A laundry room that never drops back into that band between loads becomes a standing mildew risk behind the machines and inside the washer gasket.

sections.heading: How we pick laundry room dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We don't lab-test. We compare DOE capacity ratings, ENERGY STAR listings and manufacturer manuals for drainage options, pump lift and filter design, use independent noise measurements where they exist, and read owner reviews for clogging, leaks and filter complaints. We also check CPSC recall records.

For laundry rooms, we weighted **drainage** first — a unit that can feed a standpipe is far more useful than one that needs emptying after every load — then filter cleanability, footprint and right-sized capacity.

sections.heading: What to look for in a laundry room dehumidifier

items.label: A continuous-drain port
items.text: If a standpipe or floor drain sits below the unit, a gravity hose is the simplest setup.

items.label: A pump if the drain is higher
items.text: No drain below the unit? A built-in pump lifts water to a sink or standpipe a gravity hose can't reach.

items.label: Capacity for the space
items.text: A closed closet is fine with 20–22 pints; a laundry area open to a basement or mudroom needs about 50. Our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) helps you check.

items.label: A rinseable filter
items.text: Lint clogs intakes. Choose a filter you can pull and wash in seconds.

items.label: A humidity target
items.text: Set it to 45–50% so it cycles off once the room recovers after a load.

sections.heading: How to set up a dehumidifier in a laundry room

items: Place the unit a foot or more from walls and the dryer exhaust, on a level surface.
Attach a garden-style hose to the drain port and run it **downhill** into the standpipe, sink or floor drain. Secure the end so it can't pop out when the washer drains.
Keep the hose free of kinks and loops that could trap water.
Set the humidistat to 45–50% and choose continuous drainage mode if your model has one.
Rinse the filter every couple of weeks; lint builds up faster here than in other rooms.
Leave the washer door open between loads so the drum and gasket dry out.

blocks.title: Standpipe tip
blocks.text: A dehumidifier hose only needs to sit loosely inside the standpipe, like the washer's own drain hose. Don't seal it in — an air gap prevents back-siphoning when the washer empties.
Air-drying clothes indoors instead of using the dryer? That's a different job; see our [best dehumidifier for drying clothes](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-drying-clothes/) guide.

For most homes, the **Frigidaire FFAD2233W1** is the best laundry room dehumidifier: right-sized, quiet, easy to clean and ready to drain into the standpipe you already have. If the drain isn't below the unit, get the **hOmeLabs HME1003** with its pump. Choose the collapsible **Midea Cube 20** for a stacked-washer closet, the **GE APYR50LC** for a laundry corner that opens onto a basement or mudroom, and the **Pro Breeze PB-03** for a small closet that just needs to stop smelling musty.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for a laundry room?
faqs.a: The Frigidaire FFAD2233W1 for most closed laundry rooms: a 22-pint-class unit with a washable filter and a continuous-drain port. If there's no drain below where it sits, choose a pump model like the hOmeLabs HME1003.

faqs.q: Do I need a dehumidifier in my laundry room?
faqs.a: If the room smells musty, the window fogs on wash days or a hygrometer reads above 50–55% hours after a load, yes. First make sure the dryer vent is connected and clear, since a leaky vent is a common hidden cause.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier for a laundry room?
faqs.a: A closed laundry room or closet usually needs 20–22 pints a day. If the laundry area opens onto a basement or mudroom, step up to a 35- to 50-pint unit.

faqs.q: Can a dehumidifier drain into a washing machine standpipe?
faqs.a: Yes. Run a hose from the continuous-drain port downhill into the standpipe and leave the end loose, not sealed, so there's an air gap. If the standpipe opening is higher than the drain port, you'll need a pump model.

faqs.q: Where should a dehumidifier go in a laundry room?
faqs.a: Near the drain, a foot or more from walls and away from the dryer's exhaust, on a level surface where it won't get splashed. Our [where to place a dehumidifier](/guides/where-to-place-a-dehumidifier/) guide has more tips.

faqs.q: Does a dehumidifier help dry clothes in a laundry room?
faqs.a: Yes. Running one in a closed room with a drying rack speeds drying and keeps the room from turning damp and musty, often using less energy than a full dryer cycle.
